Core idea: Tieto quantifiers hovoria o celom množstve, väčšine, dvoch možnostiach, jednej z dvoch, ani jednej z dvoch a neurčitom výbere.
Main rule / explanation: All = celá skupina. Most = väčšina. Both = dve spolu. Either = jedna z dvoch. Neither = ani jedna. Any závisí od kontextu. No + noun. None stojí samostatne.
Form / structure: all + noun. most + noun / most of + determiner. both + plural / both of. either/neither + singular alebo of + plural pronoun. no + noun. none bez noun.
When / why we use it: Na porovnanie množstva v celej skupine, väčšiny a možností výberu.
Examples:
All the employees attended. → Všetci zamestnanci prišli.
Most people agreed. → Väčšina ľudí súhlasila.
Both options are possible. → Obe možnosti sú možné.
Either option is acceptable. → Ktorákoľvek z dvoch možností je prijateľná.
Neither option works. → Ani jedna z dvoch možností nefunguje.
You can choose any option. → Môžeš si vybrať ktorúkoľvek možnosť.
No employees were available. → Nebol k dispozícii žiadny zamestnanec.
None of the employees were available. → Ani jeden zo zamestnancov nebol k dispozícii.
Special cases / exceptions: None nestojí priamo pred noun: none of the students, ale no students. Most of + specific group používa determiner.
Common mistakes:
❌ none students → ✅ no students / none of the students.
❌ Both of three options → ✅ Both of the two options / all three options.
Don't confuse with: Najprv spočítaj skupinu a urč, či ide o konkrétnu skupinu.
Quick summary / memory hook:
all = celé.
most = väčšina.
both = 2 spolu.
either = 1 z 2.
neither = 0 z 2.
no + noun.
none = pronoun.

Lesson / Topic: When I do vs When I have done – Future time clauses
Core idea: У future time clauses після when, once, as soon as, after, before та until зазвичай використовуємо Present. Іноді Present Perfect потрібен, щоб підкреслити завершення першої дії.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple показує нейтральну послідовність майбутніх подій. Present Perfect підкреслює, що перша дія буде повністю завершена перед другою.
Form / structure: When I finish the report, I'll send it. / When I have finished the report, I'll send it.
When / why we use it: Використовуй Present Simple для нейтральної послідовності. Використовуй Present Perfect, коли важливо підкреслити завершення. У main clause можливий will.
Examples:
When I finish the report, I'll send it. → Коли я закінчу звіт, я його надішлю.
When I have finished the report, I'll send it. → Коли я вже закінчу звіт, я його надішлю.
As soon as we have received the data, we will start the analysis. → Щойно ми отримаємо дані, ми почнемо аналіз.
Special cases / exceptions: Не став will усередині standard future time clause: When I will finish... неправильно. Present form отримує future meaning завдяки connector.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will finish, I'll send it. → ✅ When I finish, I'll send it.
❌ When I have finish... → ✅ When I have finished...
Don't confuse with: finish = нейтральна sequence. have finished = підкреслене completion before next event.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Future time clause → Present, не will.
Present Simple = sequence.
Present Perfect = completion emphasized.

Core idea: Have може бути звичайним смисловим дієсловом або допоміжним дієсловом. Роль визначає вся конструкція.
Main rule / explanation: Як main verb, have означає володіння, досвід або участь: I have a car. Як auxiliary, have утворює Perfect: I have finished.
Form / structure: Main verb: have + noun. Questions/negatives: do/does/did + have. Auxiliary: have/has/had + V3.
When / why we use it: Визначай роль have за конструкцією: як main verb воно називає володіння, досвід чи участь; як auxiliary будує Perfect.
Examples:
I have a car. → У мене є машина.
She has breakfast at seven. → Вона снідає о сьомій.
Do you have a minute? → У вас є хвилинка?
I don't have enough information. → У мене недостатньо інформації.
I have solved the problem. → Я розв’язав проблему.
They will have completed the work by Friday. → До п’ятниці вони завершать роботу.
Special cases / exceptions: Коли have вже є auxiliary у Perfect, do не потрібен: Have you finished? Have є частиною perfect construction і стоїть перед V3.
Common mistakes:
❌ Do you have finished? → ✅ Have you finished?
❌ Did she has a meeting? → ✅ Did she have a meeting?
❌ I have solved the problem = main verb. → Тут have — auxiliary, а solved = V3.
Don't confuse with: Подивися на слово після have: noun → часто main verb; V3 → auxiliary у Perfect.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have + noun = main verb.
have/has/had + V3 = Perfect auxiliary.
Do with have лише тоді, коли have — main verb.

Core idea: Have kann entweder ein Vollverb oder ein Hilfsverb sein. Welche Funktion es hat, hängt von der gesamten Konstruktion ab.
Main rule / explanation: Als Vollverb bedeutet have je nach Kontext zum Beispiel besitzen, erleben oder einnehmen/haben. In Fragen und Verneinungen steht bei der gewöhnlichen Vollverb-Verwendung do/does/did. Als Hilfsverb bildet have/has/had die Perfect-Zeitformen.
Form / structure: Main verb: have + noun. Questions/negatives: do/does/did + have. Auxiliary: have/has/had + V3.
When / why we use it: Entscheide zuerst, ob have die eigentliche Bedeutung trägt oder eine Perfect-Konstruktion bildet.
Examples:
I have a car. → Ich habe ein Auto.
She has breakfast at seven. → Sie frühstückt um sieben Uhr.
Do you have a minute? → Hast du eine Minute?
I don't have enough information. → Ich habe nicht genug Informationen.
I have solved the problem. → Ich habe das Problem gelöst.
They will have completed the work by Friday. → Sie werden die Arbeit bis Freitag abgeschlossen haben.
Special cases / exceptions: Bei have als Hilfsverb steht kein do/does/did: Have you finished? Bei have als Vollverb ist do/does/did in Fragen und Verneinungen üblich.
Common mistakes:
❌ Do you have finished the report? → ✅ Have you finished the report?
❌ I haven't a car. (in modern standard English usually) → ✅ I don't have a car.
Don't confuse with: Frage: Ist have das Hauptverb oder ein Hilfsverb für Perfect?
Quick summary / memory hook:
have als Vollverb = Besitz/Erfahrung usw.
have/has/had + V3 = Perfect.
Bei Vollverb have: do/does/did in Fragen/Verneinungen.

Core idea: Have puede ser un verbo principal con significado propio o un verbo auxiliar. Su función depende de toda la construcción.
Main rule / explanation: Como verbo principal, have expresa posesión, experiencia o participación: I have a car. Como auxiliar, have forma los tiempos Perfect: I have finished.
Form / structure: Verbo principal: have + noun. Preguntas/negaciones: do/does/did + have. Auxiliar: have/has/had + V3.
When / why we use it: Do you have a minute? / I don't have enough information. / I have finished the report. / She had already left.
Examples:
I have a car. → Tengo un coche.
She has breakfast at seven. → Ella desayuna a las siete.
Do you have a minute? → ¿Tiene usted un minuto?
I don't have enough information. → No tengo suficiente información.
I have solved the problem. → He resuelto el problema.
They will have completed the work by Friday. → Para el viernes habrán terminado el trabajo.
Special cases / exceptions: Cuando have ya es auxiliar en Perfect, no usamos do: Have you finished? Have forma parte de la construcción de perfecto y va seguido de V3.
Common mistakes:
❌ Do you have finished? → ✅ Have you finished?
❌ Did she has a meeting? → ✅ Did she have a meeting?
❌ I have solved the problem = verbo principal. → Aquí have es auxiliar y solved = V3.
Don't confuse with: Fíjate en la palabra que sigue a have: un noun suele indicar verbo principal; V3 indica auxiliar de Perfect.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have + noun = verbo principal.
have/has/had + V3 = auxiliar de Perfect.
Do con have solo cuando have es verbo principal.

Special cases / exceptions: Lorsque have est déjà l’auxiliary du Perfect, do n’est pas nécessaire : Have you finished? Have fait partie de la construction perfect et est suivi de V3.

❌ Did she has a meeting? → ✅ Did she have a meeting?
❌ I have solved the problem = main verb. → Ici have est un auxiliary, solved = V3.
Don't confuse with: Regarde le mot qui suit have : noun → souvent main verb ; V3 → auxiliary du Perfect.
Quick summary / memory hook:

Lesson / Topic: Clauses of contrast, purpose, reason and result
Core idea: Сполучні конструкції показують, як одна ідея пов’язана з іншою: contrast, purpose, reason або result.
Main rule / explanation: Contrast: although/even though/whereas/while. Purpose: to/in order to/so that. Reason: because/since/as. Result: so/therefore/as a result/such...that/so...that.
Form / structure: although + clause. to + V1. because + clause. so/therefore + result. such...that / so...that.
When / why we use it: Обираємо linking structure за логічним зв’язком, а не за буквальним перекладом.
Examples:
Although the task was difficult, we completed it. → Хоча завдання було складним, ми його виконали.
We changed the process to reduce errors. → Ми змінили процес, щоб зменшити кількість помилок.
We stayed inside because it was raining. → Ми залишилися всередині, бо йшов дощ.
The system was overloaded, so the service became slow. → Система була перевантажена, тому сервіс став повільним.
It was so busy that we had to wait. → Було так багато роботи, що нам довелося чекати.
Special cases / exceptions: After although/even though потрібен clause. After despite/in spite of — noun або V-ing. Purpose і result відповідають на різні запитання.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was expensive, but we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
❌ Despite it was expensive... → ✅ Despite the high price... / Despite being expensive...
Don't confuse with: Purpose = навіщо? Reason = чому? Result = що вийшло? Contrast = що несподівано відрізняється?
Quick summary / memory hook:
although/even though = contrast.
to/in order to/so that = purpose.
because/since/as = reason.
so/therefore/as a result = result.

Lesson / Topic: Clauses of contrast, purpose, reason and result
Core idea: Verbindungsstrukturen zeigen, wie eine Idee mit einer anderen zusammenhängt: contrast, purpose, reason oder result.
Main rule / explanation: Für contrast verwenden wir z. B. although. Für purpose steht oft to + V1. Für reason verwenden wir because + clause. Für result sind so, therefore, such...that und so...that typische Strukturen. Der Begriff V-ing bleibt dabei als englische Formbezeichnung erhalten.
Form / structure: although + clause. to + V1. because + clause. so/therefore + result. such...that / so...that.
When / why we use it: Wähle die Struktur nach der logischen Beziehung zwischen den beiden Aussagen.
Examples:
Although the task was difficult, we completed it. → Obwohl die Aufgabe schwierig war, haben wir sie erledigt.
We changed the process to reduce errors. → Wir haben den Prozess geändert, um Fehler zu reduzieren.
We stayed inside because it was raining. → Wir blieben drinnen, weil es regnete.
The system was overloaded, so the service became slow. → Das System war überlastet, deshalb wurde der Service langsam.

Main rule / explanation: Present unreal: wish/if only + Past Simple. Past regret: + Past Perfect. Would rather about another person + Past Simple. It's time + Past Simple môže odkazovať na prítomnosť/blízku budúcnosť.
Form / structure: wish + V2. wish + had + V3. would rather + person + Past Simple. it's time + Past Simple.
When / why we use it: Na vyjadrenie nereálnej prítomnosti, ľútosti nad minulosťou, preferencie týkajúcej sa inej osoby alebo toho, že je čas konať.
Examples:
I wish I knew the answer. → Kiežby som poznal odpoveď.
If only I had more time. → Keby som mal viac času.
I wish I had prepared better. → Kiežby som sa bol lepšie pripravil.
I'd rather you didn't tell them yet. → Radšej by som bol, keby si im to zatiaľ nepovedal.
It's time we left. → Už je čas odísť.
Special cases / exceptions: Past form tu nemusí znamenať minulý čas. Ukazuje odstup od reality.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish I know the answer. → ✅ I wish I knew the answer.
❌ It's time we leave. → ✅ It's time we left.
Don't confuse with: Past form neprekladaj doslova ako minulosť. Sleduj funkciu: unreal, regret, preference, urgency.

wish + Past = nereálna prítomnosť.
wish + Past Perfect = ľútosť nad minulosťou.

Lesson / Topic: Unless, even if, provided, as long as, etc. – Other expressions in conditionals
Core idea: Unless, even if, provided/providing та as long as виражають різні типи умов.
Main rule / explanation: Unless = if not. Even if = результат не зміниться за цієї умови. Provided/providing і as long as = умова має бути виконана.
Form / structure: unless + Present. even if + Present. provided/providing/as long as + clause.

Examples:

Special cases / exceptions: Не став will після unless/if у future condition clause: Unless it rains, we'll go.

❌ Even if it will be difficult, we'll continue. → ✅ Even if it is difficult, we'll continue.
Don't confuse with: Unless = negative condition. Even if = умова не змінює result. Provided/as long as = required condition.

Lesson / Topic: Modal verbs – permission, obligation, prohibition, necessity
Core idea: Modal verbs можуть виражати permission, obligation, prohibition та absence of necessity. Значення змінюється залежно від modal/semi-modal.
Main rule / explanation: Must = strong obligation. Have to = часто external rule. Mustn't = prohibition. Don't have to/needn't = no necessity. Can/may = permission. Be allowed to = permission across tenses.
Form / structure: must/have to/mustn't/don't have to/needn't + V1. can/may + V1. be allowed to + V1.
When / why we use it: Використовуй, коли потрібно виразити obligation, prohibition, no necessity або permission, зокрема в різних часах.
Examples:
You must wear a badge. → Ви повинні носити бейдж.
We have to submit the form by Friday. → Ми повинні подати форму до п’ятниці.
You mustn't share this password. → Не можна повідомляти цей пароль.
You don't have to attend. → Вам не обов’язково бути присутнім.
You may leave early. → Ви можете піти раніше.
We weren't allowed to enter. → Нам не дозволили увійти.
Special cases / exceptions: Mustn't і don't have to не є протилежностями: prohibition vs optional action.
Common mistakes:
❌ You mustn't go = «тобі не потрібно йти». → Ні: «тобі заборонено йти».
❌ You don't have to go = «тобі заборонено». → Ні: «тобі не обов’язково йти».
Don't confuse with: Спочатку виріши: obligation, prohibition, no necessity чи permission?
Quick summary / memory hook:
must = obligation.
have to = external requirement.
mustn't = prohibited.
don't have to/needn't = optional.
can/may = permission.

Lesson / Topic: Ellipsis and substitution – Omitting or replacing words
Core idea: Ellipsis — пропуск слів, які легко відновити з контексту. Substitution — заміна повторюваної структури іншим словом/виразом.
Main rule / explanation: Ellipsis removes understood material. Substitution uses words such as one, ones, do, so, neither to avoid repetition.
Form / structure: want to / promise to / me to etc. can leave understood words. so/neither/do/one/ones replace repeated material.
When / why we use it: Використовуй, щоб мовлення звучало природніше і не повторювало вже зрозуміле.
Examples:
I can help if you want me to. → Я можу допомогти, якщо хочеш, щоб я допоміг.
She didn't call, although she promised to. → Вона не зателефонувала, хоча обіцяла.
I need a new laptop. So does Anna. → Мені потрібен новий ноутбук. Анні теж.
I don't like the first option, but I like the second one. → Мені не подобається перший варіант, але другий мені подобається.
Special cases / exceptions: Ellipsis працює лише тоді, коли пропущену інформацію можна відновити з контексту. Не вилучай слова, якщо виникає ambiguity.
Common mistakes:
❌ I chose the blue report because the blue report was clearer. → ✅ I chose the blue report because it was clearer.
❌ Прибирати слова, які не можна відновити з контексту. → ✅ Пропускай лише те, що співрозмовник легко розуміє.

Core idea: Cleft sentences ділять інформацію на частини, щоб один елемент отримав особливий emphasis.

Lesson / Topic: Zero, first, second, and third conditionals
Core idea: Чотири major conditional patterns показують різні відношення між reality та time.
Main rule / explanation: Zero = general truth. First = real future possibility. Second = unreal/unlikely present/future. Third = unreal past. Mixed forms connect different periods.
Form / structure: Zero: If + Present, Present. First: If + Present, will + V1. Second: If + Past, would + V1. Third: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Використовуй conditional pattern відповідно до поєднання часу та reality.
Examples:
If you heat water to 100°C, it boils. → Якщо нагріти воду до 100°C, вона кипить.
If it rains, we'll stay home. → Якщо піде дощ, ми залишимося вдома.
If I had more time, I would travel more. → Якби в мене було більше часу, я б більше подорожував.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train. → Якби ми вийшли раніше, ми б встигли на потяг.
Special cases / exceptions: Choice depends on reality and time, not on the word if itself. Mixed conditionals combine periods.
Common mistakes:
❌ «Є if → завжди Second Conditional». → Ні.
❌ Every hypothetical sentence is Third. → Third is specifically unreal past.
Don't confuse with: Спочатку визнач: general, real future, unreal now/future чи unreal past?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Zero → general truth.
First → realistic future.
Second → unreal now/future.
Third → unreal past.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced present simple and present continuous
Core idea: Вибір Present Simple і Present Continuous на C1 залежить не лише від часу, а й від того, чи йдеться про постійну ситуацію, тимчасову дію, зміну або незвичне повторення.

Form / structure: S + V1/V-s. S + am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: She works for an international company. = stable fact. She is working from home this month. = temporary. You're always interrupting me. = repeated behaviour viewed as irritating/temporary.
Examples:
She works for an international company. → Вона працює в міжнародній компанії.
She is working from home this month. → Цього місяця вона працює з дому.
More companies are moving their services online. → Все більше компаній переводять свої послуги в онлайн.

Quick summary / memory hook:

Continuous → temporary/developing/unusual behaviour.
Meaning matters more than «now».

Core idea: Alegerea dintre Present Simple și Present Continuous depinde nu doar de timp, ci și de faptul că vorbim despre o situație stabilă, o activitate temporară, o schimbare sau o repetare neobișnuită.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple arată mai des o situație stabilă, un obicei, fapt sau stare. Present Continuous arată o situație temporară, o schimbare sau un comportament repetat văzut ca neobișnuit/iritant.
Form / structure: S + V1/V-s. S + am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Folosește forma după meaning: state, activity, temporary situation sau developing trend.
Examples:
She works for an international company. → Lucrează pentru o companie internațională.
She is working from home this month. → Lucrează de acasă luna aceasta.
More companies are moving their services online. → Tot mai multe companii își mută serviciile online.
You're always interrupting me. → Mă întrerupi mereu.
Special cases / exceptions: Unele stative verbs rămân non-continuous: understand, believe, own. Unele își schimbă sensul și pot fi continuous: I'm having lunch; I'm thinking about the proposal; We are seeing more customers this year.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am understanding the problem. → ✅ I understand the problem.
❌ She owns the company, so she is owning it. → ✅ She owns the company.
Don't confuse with: Nu alege Continuous doar pentru că acțiunea se întâmplă „acum”. Uită-te la meaning: state, activity, temporary situation sau developing trend.
Quick summary / memory hook: Simple → stable/state/repeated. | Continuous → temporary/developing/unusual behaviour. | Meaning matters more than „now”.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced past simple, past continuous & past perfect
Core idea: Продвинута робота з past tenses — це організація narrative: що є основною послідовністю, що було фоном, що сталося раніше і що тривало до минулого моменту.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = main completed events. Past Continuous = background/in-progress. Past Perfect = earlier past event. Past Perfect Continuous = duration/activity before a past point.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: She opened the file, checked the figures and sent the report. / She was checking the figures when the system crashed. / When we arrived, the meeting had already started. / She had been working for hours before she found the cause.
Examples:
She opened the file, checked the figures and sent the report. → Вона відкрила файл, перевірила цифри й надіслала звіт.
She was checking the figures when the system crashed. → Вона перевіряла цифри, коли система вийшла з ладу.
When we arrived, the meeting had already started. → Коли ми прийшли, зустріч уже почалася.
She had been working on the problem for hours before she found the cause. → Вона працювала над проблемою кілька годин, перш ніж знайшла причину.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect не потрібен автоматично для кожної earlier action. Він корисний, коли relationship between past events важливий з обраної narrative viewpoint.
Common mistakes:
❌ Використовувати Past Perfect у кожному реченні про минуле. → Потрібно показати конкретний зв’язок з іншою past point.
❌ She had been work... → ✅ She had been working...
Don't confuse with: Спочатку побудуй timeline. Past Simple = main line; Past Continuous = background; Past Perfect = earlier; Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main events.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.

Core idea: Can ja be able to väljendavad mõlemad võimet, kuid be able to muutub oluliseks teistes aegades ja aspektides ning konkreetse õnnestunud minevikusündmuse puhul. May/might väljendavad võimalikkust.
Main rule / explanation: Can = ability now. Be able to sobib future/perfect forms'ides. Could = general past ability. Was/were able to või managed to on sageli selgemad ühe konkreetse õnnestunud minevikusündmuse puhul. May/might = possibility.
Form / structure: can + V1. be able to + V1. could + V1. may/might + V1. may/might have + V3.
When / why we use it: I can solve the problem. / We'll be able to access the system tomorrow. / We were able to solve the problem. / It may be true. / She might have forgotten.
Examples:
I can solve the problem. → Ma suudan probleemi lahendada.
We'll be able to access the system tomorrow. → Homme saame süsteemile ligi.
We were able to solve the problem. → Meil õnnestus probleem lahendada.
It may be true. → Võimalik, et see on tõsi.
She might have forgotten. → Võimalik, et ta unustas.
Special cases / exceptions: Might väljendab mõnikord veidi väiksemat kindlust kui may, kuid erinevus pole alati range. Could pole alati parim one-off successful past event'i puhul.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'll can access it tomorrow. → ✅ I'll be able to access it tomorrow.
❌ We could solve the specific problem yesterday. → Sageli selgem: We were able to solve the problem.
Don't confuse with: Can/could — modal. Be able to — paindlik tense/aspect. May/might — possibility.
Quick summary / memory hook:
can → ability now.
be able to → flexible tense/aspect.
could → general past ability.
was able to/managed to → specific past success.
may/might → possibility.

Lesson / Topic: The subjunctive in English: Present and past
Core idea: English uses subjunctive-like forms mainly in formal recommendations, demands, necessity and hypothetical structures.
Main rule / explanation: Present subjunctive uses the base form after expressions such as essential, important, insist, demand: It is essential that she be present. British English often also uses should + infinitive. Past subjunctive is most visible in were.
Form / structure: that + subject + V1. Formal BrE: that + subject + should + V1. Hypothetical were: If I were..., I wish it were...
When / why we use it: It is essential that every applicant be informed. / They insisted that he leave immediately. / If I were you, I would wait.
Examples:
It is essential that every applicant be informed. → Дуже важливо, щоб кожного кандидата було поінформовано.
It is important that she be present. → Важливо, щоб вона була присутня.
They insisted that he leave immediately. → Вони наполягали, щоб він негайно пішов.
If I were you, I would wait. → На твоєму місці я б почекав.
I wish it were easier. → Шкода, що це не простіше.
Special cases / exceptions: У British English should + infinitive також поширене після таких виразів. Were у hypothetical structures позначає unreality, а не звичайний past time.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is essential that she is present. → У formal subjunctive pattern: ✅ It is essential that she be present.
❌ If I was you... → Standard formal/hypothetical: ✅ If I were you...
Don't confuse with: Subjunctive form обирається за structure і meaning, а не за звичайною послідовністю часів.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Formal recommendation/demand → base verb.
Hypothetical → were.
Past-looking form may mark unreality, not past time.

Core idea: Порядок слів можна змінювати, щоб виділити важливу частину повідомлення, протиставити ідеї або поставити довгу інформацію у зручніше місце.
Main rule / explanation: Для виділення information використовуються спеціальні конструкції: іноді частину речення виносять наперед, після negative words змінюють порядок слів, а cleft-constructions прямо показують, що саме важливо.
Form / structure: Normal order. Fronted phrase + clause. Negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject. It-cleft / What-cleft.
When / why we use it: This problem, we need to solve first. / Never have I seen such a result. / Only after the meeting did we understand the problem. / What we need is more time. / It was the deadline that caused the problem.
Examples:
This problem, we need to solve first. → Цю проблему нам потрібно вирішити першою.
Never have I seen such a result. → Я ніколи не бачив такого результату.
Only after the meeting did we understand the problem. → Лише після зустрічі ми зрозуміли проблему.
What we need is more time. → Те, що нам потрібно, — це більше часу.
It was the deadline that caused the problem. → Саме дедлайн спричинив проблему.
Special cases / exceptions: Emphasis often requires a specific syntactic pattern. Просте переміщення слів може створити ungrammatical sentence.
Common mistakes:
❌ Never I have seen... → ✅ Never have I seen...
❌ Only after the meeting we understood... → ✅ Only after the meeting did we understand...
Don't confuse with: Спочатку визнач, яка information має бути prominent, потім обирай структуру, що створює цей focus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Fronting = emphasis.
Negative/restrictive fronting → inversion.
Cleft = explicit focus.
End-weight = long information later.

The amount of traffic has increased. → Обсяг трафіку зріс.
A large quantity of water was needed. → Потрібна була велика кількість води.

❌ a number of money → ✅ an amount of money.

amount → uncountable.

Core idea: A last és next jelentése megváltozhat a the jelenlététől függően. The nélkül gyakran nowhoz viszonyított időszakot jelölnek; the-val egy sequence konkrét elemére utalnak.
Main rule / explanation: Last week = a mostani hetet közvetlenül megelőző hét. The last week of the course = a kurzus utolsó hete. Next week = a mostanit követő hét. The next week = a sequence/narrative következő hete.
Form / structure: last/next + time period. the last/the next + noun in a sequence.
When / why we use it: Döntsd el, calendar periodról beszélünk-e nowhoz képest, vagy egy konkrét sequence eleméről.
Examples:
I saw her last week. → Múlt héten láttam.
The last week of the course was difficult. → A kurzus utolsó hete nehéz volt.
I'll see you next week. → Jövő héten találkozunk.
The next week was much quieter. → A következő hét sokkal nyugodtabb volt.
Special cases / exceptions: Az article contextfüggően megváltoztatja a reference-ot.
Common mistakes: ❌ A next month és the next month mindig ugyanazt jelentik. → A context megkülönbözteti őket.
Don't confuse with:
last/next = gyakran nowhoz viszonyított kapcsolat.
the last/the next = sequence/context.
Quick summary / memory hook: Article changes the reference point.

Core idea: Lie і lay відрізняються тим, чи є дієслово intransitive «лежати», чи transitive «класти щось».
Main rule / explanation: Lie = be in a horizontal position: lie–lay–lain. Lay = put something somewhere: lay–laid–laid.
Form / structure: lie + no direct object. lay + direct object.
When / why we use it: Дивись, чи є object: I lie down. / I lay the book down.
Examples:
I need to lie down. → Мені потрібно лягти.
She is lying on the bed. → Вона лежить на ліжку.
Please lay the book on the table. → Поклади книгу на стіл.
He laid the keys on the desk. → Він поклав ключі на стіл.
Special cases / exceptions: Past of lie (recline) is lay. Lay має власний past laid. Саме це часто спричиняє confusion.
Common mistakes:
❌ Yesterday I laid on the sofa. → ✅ Yesterday I lay on the sofa.
❌ He lay the keys on the desk. → ✅ He laid the keys on the desk.
Don't confuse with: lie = position/state. lay = put something.
Quick summary / memory hook:
lie – lay – lain.
lay – laid – laid.

Special cases / exceptions: Look needs at у basic pattern, коли означає direct your eyes toward something.

see = perception.
look at = directed attention.
watch = sustained observation.

see = notice.
look at = direct eyes.
watch = observe over time.

Lesson / Topic: On the other hand vs On the contrary
Core idea: On the other hand і on the contrary обидва можуть зв’язувати ideas, але виражають різні відношення.
Main rule / explanation: On the other hand introduces another side/aspect of an issue. On the contrary directly contradicts or corrects a previous statement/assumption.
Form / structure: Sentence. On the other hand, sentence. / On the contrary, sentence.
When / why we use it: Використовуй on the other hand, коли показуєш іншу сторону; on the contrary — коли кажеш «навпаки, це не так».
Examples:
The job is well paid. On the other hand, the hours are long. → Робота добре оплачується. З іншого боку, робочий день довгий.
“I thought the task was difficult.” “On the contrary, it was quite easy.” → «Я думав, що завдання складне». «Навпаки, воно було досить легким».
Special cases / exceptions: On the contrary requires direct contradiction/correction, not merely different information.
Common mistakes:
❌ Two different facts = automatically on the contrary. → Ні; often on the other hand.
✅ On the contrary, it was easy. → direct correction.
Don't confuse with:
other hand = another aspect.
contrary = opposite of what was suggested.

on the other hand = інший аспект.

Lesson / Topic: Remember & Forget: To Do vs Doing
Core idea: Remember/forget + to V1 стосуються дії, яку потрібно/потрібно було виконати. + V-ing — memory of an action that happened.
Main rule / explanation: to-infinitive = task/action to do. V-ing = memory/experience of doing.
Form / structure: remember/forget + to + V1. remember/forget + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Порівняй: Did I remember the task? vs Do I remember the event?
Examples:
Remember to send the email. → Не забудь надіслати email.
I forgot to call him. → Я забув йому зателефонувати.
I remember meeting her. → Я пам’ятаю, як із нею познайомився.
I'll never forget visiting that place. → Я ніколи не забуду, що побував у тому місці.
I remembered to lock the door. → Я не забув замкнути двері.
I remember locking the door. → Я пам’ятаю, як замкнув двері.
Special cases / exceptions: Різниця не просто в часі. Вона в relationship between remembering and the action.
Common mistakes:
❌ I forgot meeting her. = «я забув, що мав із нею зустрітися». → ✅ I forgot to meet her. (забув зробити).
❌ I remembered meeting her. = «я згадав, що мав із нею зустрітися». → ✅ I remember meeting her. (пам’ятаю подію зустрічі).
Don't confuse with:
to do = remember/forget the task.
doing = memory of past action.
Quick summary / memory hook:
remember/forget + to do → task.
remember/forget + doing → memory.

Core idea: Τα wish, hope και expect σχετίζονται με future ή desired situations, αλλά δείχνουν διαφορετική σχέση με την πραγματικότητα.
Main rule / explanation: Hope = desired and realistically possible. Expect = believe something is likely/anticipated. Wish = unreal, unlikely or impossible situation ή regret.
Form / structure: hope + clause/to V1. expect + noun/to V1/that-clause. wish + unreal structure.
When / why we use it: Χρησιμοποιούμε τα ρήματα για να ξεχωρίσουμε realistic desire, expectation και unreal/regret.
Examples:
I hope we can finish today. → Ελπίζω να μπορέσουμε να τελειώσουμε σήμερα.
I expect the meeting to finish at five. → Περιμένω ότι η συνάντηση θα τελειώσει στις πέντε.
I wish I had more time. → Μακάρι να είχα περισσότερο χρόνο.
I wish you were here. → Μακάρι να ήσουν εδώ.
We wish you a pleasant journey. → Σας ευχόμαστε καλό ταξίδι.
Special cases / exceptions: Το Wish δεν είναι απλό συνώνυμο του hope όταν το επιθυμητό γεγονός είναι realistically possible.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish we can finish today. → Για realistic possibility: ✅ I hope we can finish today.
❌ I expect I had more time. → Για unreal present: ✅ I wish I had more time.
Don't confuse with: realistic desire → hope. likely expectation → expect. unreal/regret → wish.
Quick summary / memory hook:
hope = desired + possible.
expect = likely/anticipated.
wish = unreal/regret.
